evidence: POSTECH/KAERI demonstrated a graphene-Nafion membrane that, under an applied electric field, passes protons and holds back tritium from liquid tritiated water at room temperature (Manchester also ran pilot-scale graphene isotope separation).
Found MOF oxygen-capture reviews (incl. temperature-swing release), solar-panel oxygen concentrators and sun-driven MOF water harvesters, but nothing on a sun-heated sorbent oxygen concentrator.
Simulation studies (2015, 2025) and an ESA project propose hydrogen-loaded MOFs as spacecraft radiation shielding; no hardware.
Juhel et al. 2018 model PEGS-based early warning with proposed gravity strainmeters incl. atom interferometers; none built, only seismometer-based PEGS analysis exists.
Focal brain-cooling implants for epilepsy use thermoelectric (Peltier) or passive cooling; electrocaloric cooling appears only as a listed candidate mechanism in an implant-cooling review.
NASA Ames LightForce studies and an Australian SERC programme proposed ground-laser photon-pressure debris nudging, with tracking tests but no demonstrated nudge.
Simulations (Philip et al. 2016) and patents claim topological-insulator interconnects beat copper below ~6 nm; no demonstrated chip wiring.
Multiple theory papers model Dyakonov-Shur THz emission from hydrodynamic graphene electrons and note it has never been observed experimentally.
Gate-defined Josephson junctions and tunnelling transistors in magic-angle graphene were built (Rodan-Legrain 2021), but no superconducting logic circuit.
Room-temperature writing, current-driven motion and MTJ readout of skyrmions shown as separate lab components; no working racetrack memory.
FeMoco quantum simulation exists only as resource estimates and proposals (Reiher et al. 2016 onward); no quantum hardware has done it.
A single light-field-controlled logic gate in graphene was demonstrated (Nature 2022), but no multi-gate processor or circuit exists.
MAGIS/AION-type mid-band atom-interferometer detectors are proposed and under construction; none has detected a gravitational wave.
Micius did satellite quantum-secure time transfer via two-way QKD (not entangled pairs) and entanglement time transfer is shown only over 2 km links; no entanglement-based satellite clock sync.
Proof-of-principle entanglement/memory-assisted interferometers over 1.55-20 km fibre with lab light (Harvard, USTC 2025), but no telescope or on-sky use.
Ultrasound-guide-star (TRUE) focusing works in brain tissue and other methods image through thin mouse skull, but no ultrasound-guided neuron imaging through an intact skull.
Seeded amplification plus cryo-EM distinguished PD from MSA fibrils, but from post-mortem brain tissue; living-patient diagnosis remains a proposal.
EU AIRCOAT project applied a Salvinia-effect air-retaining foil to a research vessel and a container-ship test patch, forming an air layer with ~10% friction drag reduction in near-operational tests.
Superhydrophobic and self-healing anti-icing coatings tested in icing tunnels and on UAV propellers; no self-healing textured skin on an aircraft.
Searched for microcapsule/self-healing polymer heart valve leaflets; found only polymer-valve fatigue work and a bioresorbable valve headlined 'self-healing' without a healing mechanism.
Self-healing encapsulants (e.g. a water-resistant self-healing fluoroelastomer for implanted antennas) exist at materials level; none shown on neural implants in vivo.

Patents describe CNT polymer-concrete overlays with self-sensing and crack-triggered Joule-heating self-healing structures, and lab CNT self-sensing/heating composites exist; never combined in a deck.
CNT-reinforced flywheel rotors appear in patents, a Navy SBIR proposal and Sandia studies; no CNT-fibre rotor prototype found.
CNT-enhanced overhead conductors exist as simulations, patents and a Mitacs/bbcp research project; field trials found only for carbon-fibre-core conductors.
Rotating skyhook papers analyse CNT tether strength and payload capture; none built or flown.
